snapshot.meaning: A dated read of the deployed public record on 2026-09-04. The feed held thirteen case files, each assembled from configured sources with no hand picking. Three files are carried into this world with their real source counts, source-type splits and record state. Labels are anonymised; no subject, publisher or ingested URL is reproduced.

sharedMediaSource.note: In every file read on this date the independent-media side traced back to a single publisher. The record does not fold that into a headline. It shows the source count and the split so a reader can weigh how many points of view stand behind a file.

openQuestions.statement: No official government statement on this has been recorded as a verifiable fact yet. Only media reporting exists so far.

integrity.note: Every claim row carries a control to report an extraction issue, and the history of additions and corrections is kept and never rewritten. A source that fails is a visible workflow state, not a silent gap.

corpusBenchmark.reason: Thirteen files on one day is a snapshot, not a denominator. No repeatable corpus export with source, duplicate, freshness and unresolved-record counts is published yet, so this world shows no corpus size, coverage or clustering score.
